name: Earth
fact: Earth is the only known world with liquid water oceans on its surface and the only place known to host life.
blurb: Fully furnished blue marble with liquid oceans, breathable air and one moon included. The only known address with life already in residence, so the neighbors come standard.

name: Europa
fact: Europa likely hides a global saltwater ocean beneath its ice shell, with more water than all of Earth's oceans combined.
blurb: Icy shell over a likely global saltwater ocean holding more water than all of Earth's oceans combined. Waterfront living at 102 K on the surface, with Jupiter looming overhead.

name: Io
fact: Io is the most volcanically active body in the Solar System, with hundreds of volcanoes and lava fountains tens of kilometers high.
blurb: The most volcanically active property in the Solar System, with hundreds of volcanoes and lava fountains tens of kilometers high. Nonstop fireworks courtesy of Jupiter, no permit required.

name: Jupiter
fact: Jupiter's Great Red Spot is a storm larger than Earth that has raged for at least 190 years.
blurb: The largest lot in the neighborhood at about 318 Earths of mass, with a Great Red Spot storm raging for at least 190 years. No solid surface, so skip the open house.

name: Mars
fact: Mars hosts Olympus Mons, the tallest volcano in the Solar System at about 22 kilometers high.
blurb: Rust-red fixer-upper featuring Olympus Mons, the tallest volcano in the Solar System at about 22 kilometers. Thin air, big skies and two small moons thrown in, so pack a coat for 210 K.

name: Mercury
fact: Mercury's surface swings from about 700 K in daylight to about 100 K at night. It completes a year in 88 days.
blurb: Compact starter planet on the fastest orbit in the neighborhood, with a full year in just 88 days. Daytime heat near 700 K, nighttime chill near 100 K, and no atmosphere to soften either.

name: Moon
fact: The Moon is slowly drifting away from Earth at about 3.8 centimeters per year.
blurb: Quiet lot beside Earth with no atmosphere and just 0.165 g, so every step is a bounce. It drifts about 3.8 centimeters farther away each year, for ever more privacy.

name: Neptune
fact: Neptune has the fastest winds measured in the Solar System, above 2,000 kilometers per hour, and diamond rain is thought to fall deep inside.
blurb: Deep blue ice giant with the fastest winds measured in the Solar System, above 2,000 kilometers per hour. Remote enough for total privacy, with one lap around the Sun every 165 years.

name: Pluto
fact: Pluto was discovered in 1930 and has a heart-shaped plain of nitrogen ice called Sputnik Planitia. One year there lasts 248 Earth years.
blurb: Beloved former planet with a heart-shaped plain of nitrogen ice called Sputnik Planitia. At 44 K, it is a 248-year wait for your first anniversary.

name: Saturn
fact: Saturn is less dense than water, so it would float in a large enough bathtub. Its rings are mostly water ice.
blurb: Rings included at no extra charge, made mostly of water ice. Less dense than water, it would float in a big enough bathtub, and with hundreds of moons the guest parking is covered.

name: Sun
fact: The Sun holds about 99.8 percent of the Solar System's mass. Its light takes 8 minutes and 20 seconds to reach Earth.
blurb: Anchor property of the whole neighborhood, holding 99.8 percent of the Solar System's mass with a glowing 5,800 K finish. Sunlight reaches Earth in about 8 minutes, so the view is basically instant.

name: Titan
fact: Titan is the only moon with a thick atmosphere and the only other world known to have liquid lakes and seas, made of methane and ethane.
blurb: The only moon with a thick atmosphere, plus lakes and seas of liquid methane and ethane. Hazy orange skies, Saturn on the horizon, and a lakefront that sits at a chilly 94 K.

name: Uranus
fact: Uranus spins on its side with an axial tilt of about 98 degrees, and lab experiments suggest diamonds may rain inside it.
blurb: Sideways-spinning ice giant tilted about 98 degrees, for seasons that last roughly 21 years each. Cool blue finish, possible diamond rain deep inside, and a very private 59 K.

name: Venus
fact: Venus has the hottest surface of any planet, about 737 K under 92 atmospheres of carbon dioxide. Its day is longer than its year.
